prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Disable CTS sink clustering (size/diameter = 0) so the clock tree is built without clustering-induced detours and extra buffers; this reduces clock insertion delay/skew and clock-buffer congestion, leaving more routing resources and slack headroom for the propagated-clock setup paths that determine full-flow WNS/TNS, while keeping overflow well under 300.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.010 robust(mean-std)=-0.032 min_case=-0.037 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.037 dWNS=-15.8% dTNS=+4.5% overflow~99
  bp-ng45: score=-0.003 dWNS=-8.9% dTNS=+5.6% overflow~122
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.049 dWNS=-3.1% dTNS=+10.1% overflow~100
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis not supported: disabling CTS sink clustering worsened WNS in all three cases (dWNS −15.8%, −8.9%, −3.1%), with only TNS improving slightly (+4.5%, +5.6%, +10.1%) and overflow staying low (~99–122). The WNS degradation suggests removing clustering increased clock insertion delay/skew or buffer count rather than reducing detours, hurting propagated-clock setup paths. Next step: sweep small nonzero size/diameter values (e.g., 5–20 µm) to retain clustering benefits while trimming detours, and re-evaluate WNS/TNS.
